entries.name: Grants
answered
entries.summary:
Carries out one request line and returns the response line.

It does not fail: a request that cannot be parsed, or is not allowed, gets an `{"ok":false}` response that says why.

entries.name: host
entries.summary:
Returns the lower-cased host name of an `http` or `https` URL.

Any other scheme is an error, and so is a URL with user information before the host (`https://user@host/`), which could disguise the real host.

entries.name: root
entries.summary: Returns the cache directory: `TEY_CACHE`, or `~/.cache/tey`, or `.tey-cache` when `HOME` is not set.

entries.name: packagePath
entries.summary:
Returns where a dependency's package lives in the cache.

A Git checkout is stored under a hash of its URL and then its commit, so two packages with the same name from different sources never share one. A `path` dependency's location comes from `Tey.Snapshot`.

entries.name: fetch
entries.summary:
Makes sure a dependency is in the cache, cloning it at its locked commit if needed, and returns its package path.

A workspace package is an error, since it is never cached.

entries.name: verify
entries.summary:
Checks that a cached dependency matches the SHA-256 in the lockfile, and returns its package path.

It is an error when the dependency is not cached, or when `git archive` of its commit hashes to something else.

entries.name: parser
entries.summary:
Returns Tey's built-in options and commands as one `OptionConfig`.

`OptionParser` matches the command words, removes them, and passes the rest to the handler. The help text and the dispatch come from this one list, so they cannot disagree.

entries.name: cli
entries.summary:
Returns the parser Tey runs: `parser` plus one command for each `command(...)` in the current package's manifest.

Because they are declared like the built-ins, package commands appear in `tey help` and in the unknown-command message. They cannot shadow a built-in, since the manifest reader rejects those names (`Tey.Manifest.reservedCommands`), and they are listed under their own "Package commands" heading so a reader knows to look in package.kex.

entries.name: dispatch
entries.summary:
Runs the Tey command line `args` and returns the exit code.

The color flags are handled first, by setting `NO_COLOR`. The line is then parsed once to answer what `run` cannot, namely whether it asks for `--version` and whether it names a built-in command, and handed to `run`, which parses it again and dispatches. A parse error is left for `run` to report with the help text.

entries.name: colorFlag?
entries.summary:
Returns whether `argument` turns colors off.

Both `--no-color` and `--no-colors`, the spelling `kex` uses, are accepted.

entries.name: plain?
entries.summary:
Returns whether `args` asks for output without colors.

Only arguments before a bare `--` count; those after it belong to the program being run, which may have a `--no-color` of its own.

entries.name: withoutColorFlags
entries.summary:
Returns `args` without the color flags before any bare `--`.

`dispatch` handles those flags itself by setting `NO_COLOR`, which `Console`, every child `kex` and the parser's error text all read. Removing them here makes the flag work anywhere on the line, including after `tey docs`, whose own parser does not know it.

entries.name: relayColors
entries.summary:
Sets `FORCE_COLOR` so every `kex` that Tey starts uses colors when Tey does.

It does nothing when colors are off or `NO_COLOR` is set, so `NO_COLOR` still wins in every child. `Kex.AST` passes `--no-colors`, which overrides this, so output Tey parses back has no escape codes.

entries.name: announceToolchain
entries.summary:
Sets `KEX` to the compiler Tey selected, so the rest of the process uses it.

`Kex.AST`, which reads `package.kex`, runs the compiler named by `KEX` and otherwise whatever `kex` is on PATH. Tey is started by `erl`, not by `kex`, so without this a manifest would be read by an unrelated compiler, or by none when `kex` lives only inside the Tey home. A `KEX` that is already set is left alone.

entries.name: install
entries.summary:
`tey install` in a package: installs its dependencies, then its targets.

`--without dev` skips fetching a group's dependencies. The lockfile still lists them, so dropping the flag later needs no new resolve.

entries.name: installWorkspace
signatures: installWorkspace(without: String, packageName: String, force?: Bool, approveAll?: Bool) -> Integer
entries.summary: Does what `install` does. `force?` lets targets replace programs Tey does not own (see `Tey.Programs.refusal`), and `approveAll?` approves every plugin without asking.

entries.name: installDependencies
signatures: installDependencies(context: Context, without: String, approveAll?: Bool) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary: Does everything `tey install` does before building: resolves the workspace's lock or reuses it, fetches and verifies what it names, approves plugins, and writes the lock.

entries.name: installPrograms
entries.summary: `tey install <argument>...`: installs a program from a path or a Git URL, or updates installed programs by name. Several arguments must all be names, since a source is one program with its own options.

entries.name: reinstallProgram
entries.summary:
`tey install <name>`: updates an installed program by installing it again from the source its receipt records.

A tag or an exact commit stays pinned unless a new `--tag`, `--branch` or `--ref` is given. A branch, HEAD or path is rebuilt only when its commit or content changed, unless `--rebuild` asks for it, say after an Erlang upgrade or a compiler fix.

entries.name: uninstallPrograms
entries.summary: `tey uninstall <name>...`: removes the programs each receipt owns, then the receipt and its build tree. A program since replaced by a file Tey did not write is left in place, with a message.

entries.name: installFromPath
entries.summary: Installs the program at `path` without writing to it. The workspace around it is copied to a staging directory, which gets its own lock, dependencies and build, and replaces the program's previous build tree only once its programs are installed. The checkout gains no `ebin/` and no `tey.lock`.

entries.name: installFromGit
entries.summary: Installs a program from a Git repository, at the commit `--tag`, `--branch` or `--ref` names, or at the default branch's HEAD. The commit is fetched into the cache like a dependency and installed from there like a path, so nothing is built inside the cache.

entries.name: previousApprovals
entries.summary: Returns the plugin approvals recorded in the lock of program `name`'s previous install, or none for a first install.

entries.name: programMember
signatures: programMember(context: Context, packageName: String) -> Result<Member, String>
entries.summary: Returns the workspace member a program install is for: the one `--package` names, or else the one the path is inside.

entries.name: installProgramMember
signatures: installProgramMember(context: Context, member: Member, options: InstallOptions, origin: Receipt) -> Integer
entries.summary: Finishes a path or Git install once the member is known: refuses a library, checks `--target`, then stages, builds and installs the programs.

entries.name: installStaged
signatures: installStaged(context: Context, member: Member, staging: String, options: InstallOptions, origin: Receipt) -> Integer

entries.name: dependencyClosure
entries.summary: Returns `roots` and every package they depend on, directly or not, in the newly resolved graph: the names an update affects.

entries.name: mergeUpdate
signatures: mergeUpdate(previous: LockState, fresh: LockState, roots: [String], wholeWorkspace?: Bool) -> LockState
entries.summary: Returns the lock after an update: the fresh workspace data and the fresh resolutions for `roots` and what they depend on, with every other external pin kept as it was. With `wholeWorkspace?` everything is fresh. Existing approvals are carried over; `approvePlugins` later drops those that no longer match a declaration.

entries.name: lockReusable?
signatures: lockReusable?(state: LockState, manifestFingerprint: String, toolchain: Tey.Toolchain.ToolchainInfo) -> Bool

entries.name: installTargetsSelected
signatures: installTargetsSelected(context: Context, packageName: String, force?: Bool = …) -> Integer

entries.name: installMemberTargets
entries.summary:
Installs the package's `target(...)` executables into `${TEY_HOME}/bin`, beside the `kex` shim, and records them in the package's receipt (see `Tey.Programs`). That directory is already on PATH for anyone who set up Tey.

A package without targets, such as a library, is left alone. Every name is checked before anything is built, so a refused install changes nothing.

entries.name: installMemberTargetsFrom
signatures: installMemberTargetsFrom(member: Member, force?: Bool, origin: Receipt, selected: [String]) -> Integer
entries.summary:
Does what `installMemberTargets` does, but records `origin`'s source in the receipt, since a program built in a staging copy came from somewhere else.

`selected` limits the targets installed (`--target`); empty means all.

entries.name: releaseTarget
signatures: releaseTarget(owner: String, name: String) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary: Removes `name` from `owner`'s receipt after another package took it over with `--force`. A receipt left owning nothing is deleted.

entries.name: recordInstall
signatures: recordInstall(package: ManifestPackage, origin: Receipt, installed: [String], receipts: [Receipt], claims: [(String, Claim)]) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary: Writes the package's receipt. Names taken over with `--force` are removed from the other package's receipt, and targets the previous receipt owned but this install no longer declares are deleted from the bin directory.

entries.name: dependencyRoots
entries.summary: Returns a `--source-root` for every fetched dependency of the workspace around the working directory, so `using Greet` can find it. A dependency the lockfile names but the cache lacks is reported, with `tey install` as the fix.

entries.name: dependencyRootsAt
entries.summary: Does what `dependencyRoots` does for the workspace around `start`. A program installed from a path is built in a staged copy, while the working directory may be another project with its own lockfile.

entries.name: sourceDirectoryAt
entries.summary: Returns the directory, relative to the package, that its module names are resolved against. That is `src`, or `.` when package.kex lists top-level source folders with `sources(["app", "config", "db"])`, so that `App.Models.User` is `./app/models/user.kex`. An unreadable manifest gives `src`; callers report the manifest problem themselves.

entries.name: sourceUnit
entries.summary: Returns a file in the source directory as a path relative to the package, the form the compiler is given. A directory of `.` adds nothing in front.

entries.name: sourceUnit?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when a file directly under the source directory is a module to compile. When the package itself is the source directory, its manifests are there too and are skipped.

entries.name: sourceRoots
entries.summary: Returns every `--source-root` a compile of this package needs: its own source directory first, then each dependency's. The order means a module name defined both in the package and in a dependency refers to the package's own module.

entries.name: librarySources
entries.summary: Returns a library's compilable units: every `.kex` file directly under its source directory. Subdirectories are not searched, since a nested module is reached through the file that uses it, and naming it as well would compile it twice and report a duplicate module.

entries.name: librarySourcesAt
entries.summary:
Does what `librarySources` does for the package at `packageRoot`, with the units relative to it. Run the compiler with `packageRoot` as the working directory.

The paths are relative because the compiler registers a module's declarations twice when an entry file is given as an absolute path that is also under a `--source-root`, and then reports a function as "defined twice".

entries.name: backendFlags
entries.summary:
Returns the backend flags for `tey run` and `tey test`: none, so they compile and run on the BEAM like the build that ships, or `-R` for the interpreter when `--interpret` is given.

Processes, `BEAM.*` interop and the String and Char representation differ between the two backends, so a passing interpreter run says little about the built package. `--interpret` is for working around a backend gap or for debugging.

entries.name: runPackage
signatures: runPackage(extra: [String], interpret?: Bool, packageName: String = …) -> Integer

entries.name: runCommand
signatures: runCommand(command: Command, extra: [String], interpret?: Bool) -> Integer
entries.summary:
`tey <name>` for a `command(...)` the manifest declares.

A `.kex` script runs on the selected toolchain with this package's source roots, as `tey run` would, so a release script can `using` the package it releases. Anything else runs as a shell line with `sh -c`, so `command("fmt", run: "kex --format src")` behaves as it would in a terminal, pipes and `&&` included. Extra arguments are passed as `"$@"`, so the shell does not split them again.

entries.name: generate
entries.summary:
`tey generate <namespace>:<generator> [--option value ...] [--force]`

Runs a generator that a direct dependency declares in its `plugin` block. The plugin runs as a child process. It gets the invocation as one line of JSON on stdin and replies with the files it wants written. Tey writes them, only inside the workspace, and asks before replacing a file (`--force` answers yes). The child runs in the operating system's sandbox, with no network and no writing outside scratch space; `--unconfined` lifts that, with a warning.

entries.name: pluginCommand
entries.summary:
`tey plugin <namespace>:<command> [--option value ...]`

Runs a command that a direct dependency declares in its `plugin` block, limited to what the plugin declared and the user approved.

entries.name: list
entries.summary: `tey list`: prints the locked dependencies, then the programs Tey has installed. Outside a project it prints only the programs.

entries.name: buildSelected
signatures: buildSelected(packageName: String, workspace?: Bool, requestedJobs: String = …) -> Integer

entries.name: testReportingFlags
signatures: testReportingFlags(json?: Bool, list?: Bool, only: String) -> [String]
entries.summary:
Returns the compiler flags for how `tey test` reports (kexhq/kex#199).

`--json` prints one JSON record per case, with the file and line of the `it` and of any failure. `--list` prints the cases found without running them, and wins over `--json`. `--only <name>` runs one case or one group.

The flags and the records are the compiler's; Tey only passes them on. Editors run `tey test` because Tey knows the package's source roots (see docs/testing.md).

entries.name: testSpecs
entries.summary: Returns the spec files to run: the ones named on the command line, or every `spec/*.spec.kex` when none are named. Naming one runs a single suite, as an editor's per-file run button does.

entries.name: new
signatures: new(directory: String, library: Bool, agentFiles: Bool) -> Integer
entries.summary: `tey new <directory>`: creates the directory and a package in it, named after the directory's last component, so `tey new /tmp/ooo` makes `ooo`. Like `cargo new`, it makes the directory; `init` uses the current one.

entries.name: init
signatures: init(name: String, library: Bool, agentFiles: Bool) -> Integer
entries.summary:
`tey init [name]`: makes the current directory a package, such as an existing repository. Files already there are kept.

The package is named after the directory unless `name` is given, for a checkout such as `greet-main` whose package is `greet`.

entries.name: Operation
entries.summary: A change a generator plugin asks for: write a file with the given content, or delete a file. Paths are relative to the workspace.

entries.name: decode
entries.summary: Decodes the operations a generator plugin printed to stdout, in version 1 of the generator protocol (JSON). The output is only read as data, never run as Kex code.

entries.name: apply
signatures: apply(operations: [Operation], workspaceRoot: String, force?: Bool) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary: Carries out `operations` in order under `workspaceRoot`, printing each one. Overwriting or deleting an existing file asks for confirmation unless `force?` is true. Stops at the first operation that fails.

entries.name: safePath
signatures: safePath(workspaceRoot: String, path: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary: Returns the full path for a generator's relative `path`, or an error when the path is absolute, contains `..`, or leads out of the workspace through a symlink.

entries.name: pinRef
signatures: pinRef(url: String, selector: String, requested: String) -> Result<(String, String), String>

entries.name: tags
entries.summary: Returns the tags a repository publishes, newest version first. Tags that are not versions sort last. Used to resolve a range requirement and to list the Kex toolchains that can be installed.

entries.name: commitId?
entries.summary: Returns whether `text` is a full commit id: 40 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A short id is not accepted, since it could also be a ref name.

entries.name: packageManager
entries.summary:
Finds the system's package manager, so Tey can print the exact command that installs something missing. Tey never runs these commands itself, since installing system packages needs privileges it should not ask for.

Returns the package manager this system uses: "brew", "apt", "dnf", "pacman", or "" when it cannot be told. On Linux it goes by `ID` and `ID_LIKE` in `/etc/os-release`, so derivatives such as Linux Mint and Pop!_OS get Ubuntu's answer.

entries.name: installCommand
entries.summary: Returns the command that installs `packages` with `manager`, or `None` for an unknown manager. Package names differ between managers, so the caller passes the names for that manager.

entries.name: librariesHint
entries.summary: Returns how to install the shared libraries a released Kex binary loads: readline, GMP, PCRE2 and, on Linux, OpenSSL 3, under each distribution's own package names. Without a known package manager it names the libraries.

entries.name: gitHint
entries.summary: Returns how to install Git, which Tey uses to list Kex releases and to fetch Git dependencies.

entries.name: Tey.Local
signatures: set(context: Context, name: String, path: String) -> Result<String, String>
remove(context: Context, name: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary:
Local overrides: `package.local.kex` files that point a dependency at a checkout on this machine.

The files are never committed. `set` adds them to `.gitignore`, and a tracked one is an error.

entries.name: Override
entries.summary: A local override: the package name, the checkout it points at, the `package.local.kex` that declares it, and the checkout's manifest.

entries.name: load
entries.summary:
Returns the overrides declared at the workspace root and in every member.

It is an error when an override's checkout has no `package.kex` or declares a different package, when one name is overridden in more than one place, or when a `package.local.kex` is tracked by Git.

entries.name: set
signatures: set(context: Context, name: String, path: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary:
Points `name` at the checkout at `path`, in the `package.local.kex` of the current member or else of the workspace root, and returns the package name.

A relative `path` is relative to that directory. Any earlier override of the same name in that file is replaced.

entries.name: remove
signatures: remove(context: Context, name: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary: Removes the override of `name` from the file that declares it, and returns `name`.

entries.name: validateAgainstLock
entries.summary: Checks that each override matches what `tey.lock` records for its package: the same version, the same dependencies and the same plugin interfaces.

entries.name: Tey.Lockfile
entries.summary:
Encoding and decoding `tey.lock`.

The functions here are pure: they turn the file's text into a `LockState` and back, and never touch the disk.

entries.name: Dependency
entries.summary: One locked package: where it came from, the exact commit or path, and its content hash.

entries.name: LockState
entries.summary: Everything `tey.lock` records: the toolchain, the workspace and every locked package.

entries.name: encode
entries.summary: Returns the text of `tey.lock` for `lock`, with packages sorted by name.

entries.name: decode
entries.summary:
Parses the text of `tey.lock`.

It is an error when the text is not JSON, the format version is not 1, the workspace or toolchain section is missing, or a package lacks the fields its source needs.

entries.name: Command
entries.summary:
A project-specific command, run as `tey <name>`. It puts tasks such as running the linter in the manifest, where a newcomer looks, instead of a Makefile or a `bin/` script.

A name is one word, optionally grouped with a colon: `db:migrate`, `assets:build`.

entries.name: Toolchain
entries.summary:
A toolchain package: the compiler executable with the runtime and standard library it was built with, installed together so they always match. Kex's own `package.kex` declares one, so the reader must understand it for any tey command to work in the compiler's checkout.

Fields are prefixed, as in `Command`, because a bare `compiler` would be read as a function call on a receiver of unknown type before it is read as a field here.

entries.name: sourceFolder?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when `name` can be a source folder: a plain, non-hidden directory name at the package's top, not a path, since the name becomes the first part of every module in it.

entries.name: reservedCommands
entries.summary:
The command names Tey handles itself, which a `command(...)` may not take. `tey test` must mean the same in every checkout, so a manifest that redefines one fails to read.

The list lives here because the reader enforces it; `Tey.Cli` is built on this module, so taking the list from its commands would be a cycle. Keep the two in step by hand: one `.command(...)` in `Tey.Cli`, one name here. The first word is enough, so `kex` covers every `kex ...` subcommand.

entries.name: read
entries.summary:
Reads the text of a `package.kex` into a `ManifestPackage`, or returns the first problem found.

The text is parsed with `Kex.AST`, so the manifest follows the same grammar as any Kex file, comments and multi-line calls included.

entries.name: readWorkspace
entries.summary: Reads a virtual-workspace manifest: a `package.kex` whose root is `workspace`, with no package of its own. For a package that is also a workspace root, `read` returns the workspace in `manifestWorkspace`.

entries.name: readLocal
entries.summary: Reads the text of a `package.local.kex`: the `local("name", path: "...")` overrides that point a dependency at a local checkout. Returns an error for anything else in the file, or for a package overridden twice.

signatures: visibleBinding(bindings: [Binding], namespace: String, currentMember: String?) -> Result<Binding, String>
generator(binding: Binding, name: String) -> Result<PluginOperation, String>

entries.name: fingerprint
entries.summary:
Returns a fingerprint of a plugin's declared interface and requested resources, which an approval is tied to.

Changing the plugin's implementation keeps the approval; changing a capability, a command or generator schema, or the supported Tey versions needs a new one.

entries.name: validApprovals
entries.summary:
Returns the approvals whose plugin is still declared with the same fingerprint.

Used when the lock file is refreshed, so a removed plugin, or one whose interface changed, loses its approval.

signatures: visibleBinding(bindings: [Binding], namespace: String, currentMember: String?) -> Result<Binding, String>

signatures: generator(binding: Binding, name: String) -> Result<PluginOperation, String>

signatures: typedOptions(operation: Tey.Manifest.PluginOperation, supplied: {String: String}) -> Result<{String: Any}, String>

entries.name: encodeInvocation
entries.summary:
Encodes an invocation as the message Tey sends a plugin process in version 1 of the plugin protocol: one line of JSON.

The message is JSON, not Kex source, so a plugin only ever receives data, and nothing in its context can make Tey evaluate a declaration.

entries.name: typedOptions
signatures: typedOptions(operation: Tey.Manifest.PluginOperation, supplied: {String: String}) -> Result<{String: Any}, String>
entries.summary: Converts options supplied as text to the types `operation` declares for them (`String`, `Integer`, `Float` or `Bool`). Returns an error for an option the operation does not declare, or a value that does not parse as its type.

entries.name: Tey.Programs
signatures: stage(root: String, destination: String) -> Result<Void, String>
copyInto(root: String, relative: String, destination: String) -> Result<Void, String>
publishBuild(name: String, staged: String) -> Result<Void, String>
claim(target: String, packageName: String, receipts: [Receipt], exists?: Bool, teyBuilt?: Bool) -> Claim
refusal(target: String, claim: Claim, path: String, force?: Bool) -> String?
entries.summary:
Records what Tey has installed in `${TEY_HOME}/bin`, and which package owns each file there.

Every package whose targets Tey installs gets a receipt at `${TEY_HOME}/programs/<name>/receipt.json`. Ownership is decided by the receipts alone: a file in the bin directory that no receipt lists is not Tey's to overwrite or delete, and a second package declaring a target name that another package installed is refused unless `--force` is given.

Receipts are kept per package, not per program: one package can install several targets, and reinstalling or removing it acts on all of them.

entries.name: InstallOptions
entries.summary:
The options `tey install <argument>` was given: the workspace member (`--package`), the Git pin (`--tag`, `--branch` or `--ref`; a `ref` of `HEAD` when none is given), the targets (`--target`; all of them when empty), whether to take over names other packages own (`--force`), and whether to resolve dependencies again instead of using the program's committed lock (`--fresh`).

`pinned?` is true when any pin was given; reinstalling by name keeps the receipt's pin otherwise. `rebuild?` forces a rebuild even when nothing has changed.

entries.name: pinnedReason
entries.summary:
Returns the message explaining why reinstalling `receipt` by name has nothing to do, or `None` when it has to be rebuilt.

A program pinned to a tag or an exact commit stays where the user put it, and the message says how to move it. A branch, or `HEAD`, is rebuilt.

entries.name: ProgramSource
entries.summary: What the argument to `tey install` names: a path, a Git URL or the name of an installed program. It always names a program; dependencies are added with `tey add`.

entries.name: Claim
entries.summary: What installing one target name would do to the bin directory: the name is free, already this package's, an old Tey-built file to adopt, reserved for Tey, owned by another package, or a file Tey did not install.

entries.name: reservedNames
entries.summary: Returns the target names no package may take. The `kex` shim lives in the bin directory, and replacing it would change which compiler every shell runs.

entries.name: classify
entries.summary: Decides what `argument` names: a path when it starts with `.`, `/` or `~`, a Git URL when it has a scheme or looks like `git@host:owner/repo`, and otherwise the name of an installed program.

entries.name: buildDirectory
entries.summary: Returns the directory that holds a program's build tree once it is installed.

entries.name: stagingDirectory
entries.summary:
Creates a new, empty directory to build a program in before it is installed.

It sits beside `programs/`, so a half-built tree is never listed as a program, and on the same filesystem, so installing it is a rename.

entries.name: stage
signatures: stage(root: String, destination: String) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary: Copies the tree at `root` into `destination`: the files a snapshot would hold, plus a committed `tey.lock`, which a snapshot leaves out. The lock holds the dependency versions the program's author tested.

entries.name: copyInto
signatures: copyInto(root: String, relative: String, destination: String) -> Result<Void, String>

entries.name: publishBuild
signatures: publishBuild(name: String, staged: String) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary:
Replaces a program's build tree with the staged one it was just built in.

The old tree is moved aside first and deleted last, so if a step fails, one of the two trees is still in place.

entries.name: claim
signatures: claim(target: String, packageName: String, receipts: [Receipt], exists?: Bool, teyBuilt?: Bool) -> Claim
entries.summary:
Decides what installing `target` for `packageName` would do, given every receipt and whether a file of that name already exists.

`teyBuilt?` covers programs that a project's own `tey install` put in the bin directory before receipts existed. Tey wrote those itself, so they are adopted into the receipt; refusing them would make every such installation need `--force` on its next reinstall.

entries.name: refusal
signatures: refusal(target: String, claim: Claim, path: String, force?: Bool) -> String?
entries.summary:
Returns the message explaining why `claim` stops the install, or `None` when it can go ahead.

`--force` takes a name over from another package or from a file Tey did not install, but never a name reserved for Tey.

entries.name: all
entries.summary:
Returns every receipt, sorted by package name.

A receipt that cannot be parsed is skipped with a warning on stderr, since skipping it quietly would make the files it owns look unowned. A receipt file that cannot be read at all is skipped without one.

entries.name: save
entries.summary:
Writes `receipt` to its file.

The receipt is written to a file beside it and renamed into place, so a reader never sees half a receipt and a failed write leaves the old one intact.

entries.name: teyBuilt?
entries.summary: Returns whether `path` is an escript that Tey's target build wrote: its emulator line starts Kex's escript launcher, or names `kex_main` directly, as escripts built before the launcher existed do.

entries.name: listLine
entries.summary: Returns the line `tey list` prints for one installed program.

entries.name: pinText
entries.summary: Returns what a Git install is pinned to, as `tey list` shows it: a tag such as `v0.4.0`, a branch or ref with its commit such as `main (3f9c1a2)`, or a short commit id when an exact commit was asked for.

entries.name: Tey.Resolver
signatures: resolveWorkspaceWithInfo(context: Context, toolchain: Tey.Toolchain.ToolchainInfo) -> Result<LockState, String>
chooseFromTags(name: String, tags: [String], requested: String) -> Result<String, String>

entries.name: fingerprint
entries.summary: Returns a fingerprint of the workspace members' manifests and `.teyignore` files. It changes whenever the lockfile may need resolving again.

entries.name: resolveWorkspace
entries.summary: Resolves the dependencies of every workspace member into one lock state, using the active toolchain.

entries.name: resolveWorkspaceWithInfo
signatures: resolveWorkspaceWithInfo(context: Context, toolchain: Tey.Toolchain.ToolchainInfo) -> Result<LockState, String>
entries.summary: Resolves the workspace like `resolveWorkspace`, with toolchain information the caller already has. The compiler's `--info` is then queried only once per install or resolve.

entries.name: resolvePackage
entries.summary: Resolves one package's dependencies into a lock state. Fails when the active Kex or the running Erlang/OTP is older than the package or the toolchain requires.

entries.name: chooseFromTags
signatures: chooseFromTags(name: String, tags: [String], requested: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary:
Returns the tag of the newest version of `name` that satisfies `requested`.

A monorepo can tag each member separately, as `parser-v1.2.3`. When tags with the package's prefix exist, only those are considered; otherwise plain tags such as `v1.2.3` are.

entries.name: externalizeWorkspaceDependencies
entries.summary:
Rewrites the `workspace: true` dependencies of a fetched package as Git dependencies on the same repository and commit as `parent`.

In a fetched package, `workspace: true` names a sibling in that package's repository, not a member of the consumer's workspace. The sibling's subdirectory is found later.

entries.name: Limits
entries.summary:
What a plugin process may do besides reading files and computing.

A plugin is code from a dependency, run on the user's machine. When the user approves what a plugin asks for, Tey runs it inside the operating system's sandbox so it can do no more:

- it can write only under `writable`, plus the temporary directories and
  the Kex cache that compiling and running it need;
- it can use the network only when `network?` is true;
- it cannot read the usual places credentials are kept, such as `~/.ssh`.

Every process the plugin starts has the same limits.

Two permissions are coarser than they look. `Process.Run([...])` is not enforced: the plugin can start any program, though that program has the same limits. `Net.Connect([...])` opens the whole network, not just the listed hosts, because the sandbox filters by address and not by name.

entries.name: TOOL
entries.summary: The path of macOS's `sandbox-exec`, the only sandbox supported so far. On other systems `available?` is false, and a plugin runs only with `--unconfined`.

entries.name: available?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when this system has the sandbox Tey uses.

entries.name: scratch
entries.summary: Returns the directories a Kex child process always needs to write to: the temporary directories and the Kex cache.

entries.name: profile
entries.summary: Returns the sandbox profile for `limits`. Later rules win, so the profile allows everything, denies network access and file writes, allows writes back under the writable paths, then denies reading credentials.

entries.name: prefix
entries.summary: Returns the words to put in front of a command line to run it under `limits`, `sandbox-exec -f <profile>`, and the profile's path. The caller deletes the profile once the child has exited. Fails when no sandbox is available or the profile cannot be written.

entries.name: UpgradeOutcome
entries.summary:
Upgrades Tey itself (`tey upgrade`) when it was installed from a release archive by `install.sh`. A Tey installed by Homebrew is refused; upgrade it with `brew upgrade tey`.

Tey has its own version number (`tey/package.kex`), so the newest Tey is the one declared by the newest Kex release's manifest. The manifest is fetched over HTTPS from raw.githubusercontent.com with curl, or wget when curl is missing, as `Tey.Toolchain.download` does; the GitHub API is not used, so there are no rate limits. The archive is the `tey-<version>.tar.gz` that the release workflow publishes under the same tag as the Kex archives.

The result of `tey upgrade`: the version installed and where, or why nothing was installed.

entries.name: currentPrefix
entries.summary: Returns the prefix this Tey is installed under, or `None` when it is not running from an installed launcher (a source checkout, or `erl` started by hand), where there is nothing safe to overwrite. The `bin/tey` launcher exports `TEY_INSTALL_EBIN`, so a released install always knows.

entries.name: installEbin
entries.summary: Returns the launcher's own runtime directory, from `TEY_INSTALL_EBIN`, or from `TEY_EBIN` when that is unset. `TEY_EBIN` alone is not enough: it may name the Tey paired with the selected Kex (see `installPaired`), which is not the install to upgrade.

entries.name: prefixOf
entries.summary: Returns `ebin` with its trailing `/lib/kex/tey/ebin` removed. Any other path, such as a checkout's `tey/ebin`, gives `None`: there is no install prefix to upgrade in place.

entries.name: homebrewManaged?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when the install at `prefix` belongs to Homebrew, which upgrades it with `brew upgrade tey`.

entries.name: manifestVersion
entries.summary: Returns the version from the `version("...")` line of a `package.kex` manifest, read as plain text, or `None` when there is no valid one. The manifest reader does not fit here, since it compiles a local package and this text has only been downloaded.

entries.name: compareVersions
entries.summary:
Compares two version strings, for the already-newest check. A version that does not parse compares as older, so a hand-edited development version is never treated as newer than every release and can still be upgraded.

It is built on `newer?` and not `compare`: on the BEAM backend, a trait function from another module's `make ..., implement: Comparable` does not dispatch to a record from outside that module, while a plain `let` such as `newer?` can be called from anywhere.

entries.name: carryBakedErlText
entries.summary:
Returns `newLauncher` with the absolute `erl` path of `oldLauncher` carried over.

A source install (`make -C tey install`) writes an absolute `erl` path into `bin/tey`, while release archives use a bare `erl` found on `PATH`. An upgrade keeps the absolute path. In every other case (no `BAKED_ERL` line, a relative `erl`, the development placeholder) the new launcher is returned unchanged.

entries.name: tagFor
entries.summary: Returns the tag in `tags` that names a Kex version, written with or without a leading `v`. Unlike `Tey.Toolchain.releaseTag`, it takes a tag list that was fetched once, which a scan over many versions needs.

entries.name: firstSelfUpgrading
entries.summary: The oldest Tey with an `upgrade` command. Pinning an older one is refused, because that Tey could not run `tey upgrade` to come back; the installer is the way to get one.

entries.name: installedVersion
entries.summary:
Returns the version of the Tey installed at `prefix`.

That is not always the running Tey: when the selected Kex has its own Tey unpacked beside it (see `installPaired`), the launcher runs that one. Comparing the running version would then report the install as up to date while it stays old. So the installed launcher is asked directly, pointed at its own runtime. If its answer cannot be read, the running version is returned.

entries.name: upgradeLatest
entries.summary: Runs `tey upgrade`: installs the Tey declared by the newest Kex release's manifest. Only stable releases count unless `includePre` (`--pre`) is set, which reaches a pre-release Tey without knowing its number.

entries.name: upgradePinned
entries.summary: Runs `tey upgrade <version>`: installs exactly that Tey, from the newest release whose manifest declares it, looking at stable releases first and then pre-releases. Older versions are allowed, which is the way back from a bad release, but not ones older than `firstSelfUpgrading`.

entries.name: installPaired
entries.summary:
Unpacks the Tey that a Kex release ships beside that toolchain, so `bin/tey` runs it whenever that Kex is selected. Kex and Tey are released as a pair, and a pre-release is only tested as that pair. Nothing installed is replaced, not even a Homebrew keg, so `tey kex install` does this every time.

Returns the Tey version unpacked, or `None` when it was already there; a tag's contents never change.

entries.name: SemanticVersion
entries.summary: A parsed version number: `major.minor.patch` and an optional pre-release.

entries.name: SemanticVersion
entries.summary: Orders versions by number, then by pre-release: a release ranks above its pre-releases, and pre-releases are ordered by channel (`prealpha`, `alpha`, `beta`, `rc`) and then by number.

entries.name: parseVersion
entries.summary: Parses a version such as `0.4.0`, `v0.4.0-rc.1` or `1.2`, or returns `None`. A leading `v` and build metadata after a plus sign are ignored, and a missing minor or patch number counts as 0.

entries.name: release
entries.summary: Returns the release a version belongs to, so `0.4.0-rc.1` gives `0.4.0`. Text that is not a version is returned unchanged.

entries.name: stable?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when the text is a version without a pre-release part.

entries.name: satisfies?
entries.summary:
Returns `true` when the version meets every space- or comma-separated clause of `requirement` (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `=`, `^`, `~>` or a bare version). An empty requirement or `*` accepts any version.

`~> 0.3` accepts `0.3.x` and `^0.3` accepts `0.x` from `0.3` on. A pre-release meets a requirement only when some clause names a pre-release, so `~> 0.4` does not accept `0.4.0-rc.1`.

entries.name: intersect
entries.summary:
Returns a requirement met only by versions that meet both `a` and `b`, for when two packages in one graph depend on the same package.

The result joins the two with a space, since `satisfies?` requires every clause to hold: `~> 0.1` and `>= 0.1.5` give `~> 0.1 >= 0.1.5`. An empty or `*` side is dropped.

A requirement that nothing can meet, such as `~> 0.1 ~> 0.2`, is not detected here. `highest` finds it, by returning `None`.

entries.name: intersectAll
entries.summary: Returns the intersection of all the requirements, as `intersect` does for two. `[]` and `[""]` both give `""`, which accepts any version.

entries.name: versionOf
entries.summary:
Returns the version tag inside a resolved ref: `refs/tags/v0.1.1`, `v0.1.1` and `pkg-v0.1.1` all give `v0.1.1`.

A ref without a version, such as a branch name or a commit, gives `""`, which meets no requirement.

entries.name: channelRank
entries.summary:
Returns the rank of a pre-release channel: `prealpha` 1, `alpha` 2, `beta` 3, `rc` 4, and 0 for any other name.

Plain semver would order the channels alphabetically, putting `beta` before `prealpha`.

entries.name: range?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when a requested tag is a version range, such as `~> 1.2`, and `false` for an exact tag such as `v1.2.0`.

entries.name: newer?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when `a` is a newer version than `b`. A tag that is not a version counts as older than any that is, so a stray `nightly` never wins.

entries.name: newestFirst
entries.summary: Returns the versions without duplicates, newest first, with tags that are not versions at the end.

entries.name: highest
entries.summary: Returns the newest tag that meets the requirement, or `None` when none does.

entries.name: Tey.Snapshot
signatures: create(name: String, declaredPath: String, declaringRoot: String) -> Result<Tey.Lockfile.Dependency, String>

entries.name: create
signatures: create(name: String, declaredPath: String, declaringRoot: String) -> Result<Tey.Lockfile.Dependency, String>
entries.summary:
Copies a path dependency into the cache as an immutable snapshot named by its content digest, and returns its lockfile entry.

The lockfile keeps the declared path for reference, but builds use the snapshot named by `sha256`, never the live directory. Fails when the directory is missing, its `package.kex` cannot be read or names another package, or a symbolic link in it is broken or points outside it.

entries.name: cachedPath
entries.summary: Returns the cache directory of a dependency's snapshot.

entries.name: verify
entries.summary: Returns the snapshot directory of `dependency` after checking that it is in the cache and that its content still matches the locked `sha256`.

entries.name: sourceFiles
entries.summary: Returns the files a snapshot of `root` holds, relative to it and sorted: everything except VCS metadata, build output, `package.local.kex`, `tey.lock` and paths matched by `.teyignore`.

entries.name: contentDigest
entries.summary: Returns the content digest a snapshot of `root` is published under.

entries.name: Tey.Toolchain
signatures: installSource(source: String, version: String) -> Result<String, String>
download(url: String, path: String) -> Result<Void, String>
verifyArchive(archive: String, checksumUrl: String) -> Result<Void, String>
publish(staging: String, prefix: String) -> Result<String, String>

entries.name: ToolchainInfo
entries.summary:
What the selected compiler reports about itself through `kex --info`.

The version here can differ from `Kex.VERSION`, which names the compiler that built Tey itself: a project may select a newer or older compiler.

entries.name: repository
entries.summary: Returns the Git repository Tey reads Kex releases from. `TEY_KEX_REPO` overrides it, for a fork or a mirror.

entries.name: binDirectory
entries.summary: Returns the directory holding the `kex` shim. A user puts it on PATH once, and `tey kex use` repoints the shim inside it.

entries.name: selected
entries.summary: Returns the version `tey kex use` last selected, or `None`.

entries.name: installedVersions
entries.summary:
Returns the versions installed under the Tey home, newest first.

Leftover staging directories and directories without a `bin/kex` are not listed.

entries.name: binaryOf
entries.summary: Returns the path of an installed version's `bin/kex`.

entries.name: pairedTeyEbin
entries.summary:
Returns the `ebin` directory of the Tey released with a Kex version, the same path `bin/tey` reads.

It sits beside the toolchain, not inside it, because reinstalling a Kex replaces the toolchain's whole directory and a Tey running from there would lose its modules.

entries.name: availableVersions
entries.summary: Returns the released versions, newest first, read from the repository's tags. Tags that are not versions are skipped.

entries.name: latestStable
entries.summary: Returns the newest stable release, which `tey kex install` picks when no version is given. Pre-releases are left out.

entries.name: latestIncludingPreReleases
entries.summary: Returns the newest release including pre-releases, which `tey kex install --pre` picks. Before a stable release exists, this may be the only way to get one without knowing its number.

entries.name: bundled
entries.summary:
Returns the Kex bundled beside Tey, named by `TEY_BUNDLED_KEX`, or `None` when there is none.

A package manager installs it so the first `tey` command has a compiler without a long build. It is not an installation in the Tey home: `resolved` runs it where it lies, and `tey kex use <its version>` copies it into the home, after which Tey manages it like any other version.

entries.name: bundledVersion
entries.summary:
Returns the version of the bundled Kex, or `None`.

The only way to find out is to run it, so avoid calling this in a loop.

entries.name: Toolchain
entries.summary: A Kex that `tey kex use` can select: its version, the binary that runs it, and whether it is the bundled one beside Tey and not an installation in the Tey home.

entries.name: selectableToolchains
entries.summary:
Returns every toolchain `tey kex use` can select, newest first: the ones in the Tey home and the bundled one, each with the binary that runs it.

`tey kex list --installed --json` prints this. The bundled Kex is included although it is not installed, because on a fresh install it is the one a bare `kex` runs, and `tey kex use` must be able to select it.

entries.name: selectableVersions
entries.summary: Returns every version `tey kex use` can select, newest first.

entries.name: resolveSelector
entries.summary:
Turns the argument of `tey kex use` into a version number.

`latest` means the newest version already on this machine, not the newest release: `use` never downloads anything. `tey kex install` does that.

entries.name: kex
entries.summary:
Returns the compiler every Tey command runs.

It is `resolved`'s answer (`TEY_KEX`, then the selected toolchain, then the bundled Kex where it lies), or else a bare `kex` from PATH. That last one is a fallback for a source checkout: Tey cannot update it, and it may not be the version `tey kex list` reports.

entries.name: activeInfo
entries.summary:
Reads `kex --info` from the selected compiler.

Callers that need several facts read them from one call, so they cannot come from two different binaries if the selection changes in between.

entries.name: runtimeOtpFloor
entries.summary:
Returns the OTP release that compiled the selected toolchain's runtime beams, which is the oldest Erlang that can load them.

It comes from `kex --info`. It is `None` when the toolchain is too old to have `--info`, when the field is missing, or when it is `null` because the compiler was built without `erlc`. A caller should not treat any of these as an error.

entries.name: runningOtpRelease
entries.summary: Returns the OTP release of the `erl` that will run, by asking it.

entries.name: erl
entries.summary: Returns the `erl` that Tey and Kex will run. `KEX_ERL` overrides it for both, as it does for the compiler.

entries.name: resolved
entries.summary:
Returns the compiler Tey would run, or `None` when there is none.

It tries `TEY_KEX`, then the selected toolchain, then the bundled Kex. The bundled one is run where it lies, not copied into the Tey home: nothing is installed until the user asks, and Homebrew's post-install sandbox could not write to the home anyway. A selected version always wins over it.

Unlike `kex`, this has no fallback to a bare `kex` from PATH, because that `kex` is Tey's own dispatcher and would call itself.

entries.name: installBundled
entries.summary: Copies the bundled Kex into the Tey home and selects it, so Tey manages it like any other version. This only happens when the user selects the bundled version with `tey kex use`.

entries.name: selectionHealthy?
entries.summary: Returns `false` when the selected version is no longer installed, so a caller can report a missing Kex instead of failing on a path that does not exist.

entries.name: startupProblem
entries.summary:
Returns why the toolchain installed at `prefix` cannot start, or `None` when `kex --version` runs.

A release archive is a prebuilt binary that loads readline, GMP, PCRE2 and OpenSSL from the system, and on Linux needs glibc 2.38 or later. This finds a missing library right after the install, not on the first real command.

entries.name: installRelease
entries.summary:
Installs a released version and selects it, returning its prefix.

It uses the published archive for this machine when there is one, which takes seconds and needs no C++ compiler. When there is no archive for this machine it builds from source. A corrupt archive, or a release that cannot be looked up at all, is an error and does not fall back to a build.

entries.name: ArchiveFailure
entries.summary:
Why a published archive could not be installed.

`Unavailable` means there is no usable archive for this machine, and a source build may follow. `Corrupt` means the archive did not match its checksum or did not unpack. `Unreachable` means the release's tag could not be looked up.

entries.name: releaseBase
entries.summary:
Returns the base URL of the release archives.

It is derived from `repository`, so a fork only has to set `TEY_KEX_REPO`. `TEY_KEX_RELEASES` overrides it for a mirror.

entries.name: releaseTarget
entries.summary: Returns this machine's part of a release archive name, such as `macos-arm64` in `kex-0.4.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz`.

entries.name: installSource
signatures: installSource(source: String, version: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary:
Builds the Kex source tree at `source` with CMake, installs it as `version` and selects it, returning its prefix.

The compiler, runtime BEAM modules and stdlib sources are installed together, in the CMake install layout that every Tey toolchain has.

entries.name: uninstall
entries.summary:
Removes an installed toolchain and returns its former prefix.

Removing the selected version also clears the selection and removes the shim, so the caller should ask the user to select another.

entries.name: use
entries.summary: Selects an installed version, or the bundled one, and points the shim at it.

entries.name: download
signatures: download(url: String, path: String) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary:
Downloads `url` to `path` with curl, or with wget when curl is missing.

The file appears at `path` only once the download is complete. This and the helpers below are public because `Tey.SelfUpdate` (`tey upgrade`) uses them for Tey's own archives.

entries.name: verifyArchive
signatures: verifyArchive(archive: String, checksumUrl: String) -> Result<Void, String>
entries.summary:
Downloads the checksum at `checksumUrl` and checks `archive` against it.

The file is in the `<hash>  <filename>` format that sha256sum and shasum write.

entries.name: checksumOf
entries.summary: Returns the SHA-256 of the file at `path`, computed by sha256sum or shasum so the file is never read into memory.

entries.name: releaseTag
entries.summary: Returns the repository tag for `version`, either `0.3.0` or `v0.3.0`.

entries.name: versionOf
entries.summary: Returns the version a tag names, without a leading `v`, or `None` when the tag is not a version.

entries.name: publish
signatures: publish(staging: String, prefix: String) -> Result<String, String>
entries.summary:
Moves a finished staging tree to `prefix`, and returns `prefix`.

When `prefix` already holds a toolchain, the old tree is kept until the new one is in place and put back if the move fails, so a failed reinstall leaves the previous toolchain working.

entries.name: Tey.Version
entries.summary: GENERATED by tey/Makefile from tey/package.kex — do not edit.

entries.name: number
entries.summary: Tey's own version, as declared by package.kex's version(...) line.

entries.name: Tey.Workspace
signatures: select(context: Context, packageName: String, workspace?: Bool) -> Result<[Member], String>

entries.name: discover
entries.summary:
Returns the outermost workspace containing `start`, with its members.

When no `package.kex` above `start` declares a workspace, the nearest package is the only member. Paths are made absolute without resolving symlinks, and the working directory is not changed. It fails when there is no `package.kex` at or above `start`, or when two members share a name. Dependency cycles among members are reported in `warnings`.

entries.name: select
signatures: select(context: Context, packageName: String, workspace?: Bool) -> Result<[Member], String>
entries.summary:
Returns the members a workspace-aware command should act on.

A non-empty `packageName` selects that member, and is an error when none has that name. Otherwise `workspace?` (the `--workspace` flag) selects every member. Without either, a command run inside a member acts on that member, and one run at the workspace root or outside any member acts on all of them.

entries.name: dependencyLayers
entries.summary:
Returns the members in layers, each depending only on members in earlier layers.

Members caught in a dependency cycle go together in a final layer, so a command can still run them; `discover` reports the cycle as a warning.

entries.name: options
entries.summary: Returns the options and the `build`, `prose` and `serve` subcommands of `tey docs`, from which its help is generated too.

entries.name: strict?
entries.summary:
Returns `false`, after printing an error and the help, when an unknown option such as `--sorce` was left among the arguments.

OptionParser passes options it does not know on to the command, but these subcommands take none of their own, so a leftover one is a typo.

entries.name: printUsage
entries.summary: Prints the generated help followed by the list of files a build writes, and returns 0.

entries.name: outputsHelp
entries.summary: Returns the "Outputs:" help section, styled like OptionParser's own sections: a bold heading, then one aligned row per file.

entries.name: pageFor
signatures: pageFor(source: String, items: [Kex.AST.Node], header: String) -> SourcePage
entries.summary:
Builds the page for one source file.

`header` is the file's opening comment, when a blank line separates it from what follows (`Index.fileHeader`). The AST reader attaches every comment above a declaration to it, blank lines included, so the first declaration's doc starts with the file's introduction. This cuts the header off that doc and keeps it as the page's intro; otherwise algebra.kex's "Algebraic structures: ..." would be the summary of `Monoid`.

entries.name: detachHeader
entries.summary: Returns the items with the header removed from the first documented one.

entries.name: pageTitle
entries.summary:
Returns a page's title: the name of the declaration the file is about, spelled as the source spells it ("OptionParser", "FileHandle").

The title is a single top-level module if there is one, else a single top-level type, record or trait, else a declaration named like the file, else the file name in PascalCase.

entries.name: namesStem?
entries.summary: Returns `true` when `name` is the name a file stem spells, ignoring case and underscores: `file_handle` names `FileHandle` (kexhq/kex#721), and `dns` names `DNS`.

entries.name: baseSpelling
entries.summary: Returns the part of a name a file could be named after: "FileHandle<CanRead, W>" gives "FileHandle", and "FS.Path" gives "Path".

entries.name: moduleTitle
entries.summary:
Returns the title of a file with one top-level module.

The file name matters when several files share a module: data/queue.kex, set.kex and stack.kex all wrap their module in `module Data`, and titling each page "Data" would make the sidebar entries identical. So the title is the module if its last segment matches the file name ("dns.kex" gives Net.DNS), else a nested module that matches ("queue.kex" gives Data.Queue), else the top module ("mock.kex" gives Mock).

entries.name: fileStem
entries.summary: Returns the last segment of a path: "kex/ast" gives "ast".

entries.name: Pending
entries.summary: An accumulator entry: a finished entity, or a function still collecting its clauses.

entries.name: ParamSig
entries.summary: One parameter as a clause declares it. `named?` is `false` for a pattern parameter (`let repeat(0) = ...`), whose spelling is a value that a signature should not show as a name.

entries.name: mergeMakes
entries.summary: Merges make blocks with the same target in one file, appending the later block's traits and functions to the first. Two `make Queue<A>` blocks, one for the collection traits and one for `Blankable`, read as one set of functions.

entries.name: variantEntry
entries.summary: Converts one variant. It is a named function so that the element type of `v.fields` comes from `VariantInfo`, not from `VariantEntry`'s `[String]`.

entries.name: constantBinding?
entries.summary:
Returns `true` for a binding with no parameter list that is not `foul`.

A `foul` binding with no parameter list is a zero-argument function that Kex calls each time it is named: `IO.getLine` reads a new line every time, so it is documented as a function. `IO.out`, always the same handle, is a constant.

entries.name: constantFromPending
signatures: constantFromPending(p: Pending, info: Kex.AST.FunctionInfo, prefix: String) -> Pending
entries.summary: Replaces the `PendingFunction` an earlier annotation created with a constant entry, keeping its name, doc and line.

entries.name: addClause
signatures: addClause(p: Pending, info: Kex.AST.FunctionInfo, lists: [[ParamSig]]) -> Pending

entries.name: indexedFind
signatures: indexedFind(accum: [Pending], name: String, index: Integer) -> Integer?

entries.name: declaredReturn
entries.summary: Returns the return type the source declares: the annotation's result, or the inline `-> T` of an unannotated clause. The `@return` tag is checked against it (`Index.reportDocDrift`) and never shown in its place.

entries.name: finalResult
entries.summary: Returns the final result of a curried type: for `A -> (A -> T -> A) -> A` it is `A`.

entries.name: functionTypes
entries.summary: Returns the type names a function mentions: every parameter type and the result type of each annotation, without duplicates. Search uses them to find every function that takes or returns `Integer`.

entries.name: signatureTexts
entries.summary:
Returns the signatures shown for a function, one per annotation.

A signature names every parameter with its type and ends in the result: `and(a: Integer, b: Integer) -> Integer`. The names come from a clause. The types come from the annotation (flattened to the clause's arity), from the clause's inline annotations, or, for an unannotated function, from its `@param` and `@return` tags. A function with no parameters is written as its definition is (`let sum -> Number` gives `sum -> Number`); the `name : Type` form is kept for constants. A required trait function has no clause, only a type, and takes its parameter names from its `@param` tags when the counts match.

entries.name: plainSignature
entries.summary: Builds a signature from the clause alone: inline types first, then the doc tags, and bare names when neither gives a type.

entries.name: docNamedSignature
signatures: docNamedSignature(name: String, ref: Kex.AST.TypeRef, doc: Doc) -> String
entries.summary: Builds a signature for an annotation with no clause, naming the parameters from the `@param` tags when there are exactly as many tags as the type has parameters.

entries.name: annotationSigil
entries.summary: Returns the sigil an annotation was written with. A type that cannot be paired with a clause is shown as written, and `:>` is what says the receiver is implied; a plain `:` would describe a function with no receiver.

entries.name: unnamedSignature
entries.summary: Builds a signature with types but no parameter names, such as `combine(This) -> This`, or `lines -> [String]` when there are no parameters.

entries.name: paramText
signatures: paramText(name: String, typeName: String, optional: Bool) -> String

entries.name: parenthesized
entries.summary: Wraps a function type in parentheses, so a parameter reads `f: (T -> Void)`.

entries.name: displayName
signatures: displayName(p: ParamSig, index: Integer, fn: PendingFunction) -> String
entries.summary: Returns the name shown for a parameter. A pattern parameter (`repeat(0)`) shows the name its `@param` tag gives that position, or `_`, since the literal would read as an argument.

entries.name: ConversionName
entries.summary: The conversion function's name. In `value.to(String)` the argument is the type itself, so that clause's capitalised pattern is shown as written. Anywhere else a capitalised pattern is a constructor being matched (`None`) and is not shown.

entries.name: bestParams
entries.summary: Returns, of several clauses' parameter lists, the one that names the most parameters (`repeat(n: Integer)` over `repeat(0)`), with types filled in from the other clauses of the same arity.

entries.name: withPeerType
signatures: withPeerType(p: ParamSig, index: Integer, peers: [[ParamSig]]) -> ParamSig

entries.name: signatureTypeText
entries.summary: Renders a type as source would write it: arrows chain to the right without the extra parentheses `typeRefText` adds, and a function-typed parameter is parenthesized, so `(X -> Y) -> Z` stays distinct from `X -> Y -> Z`.

entries.name: flattenToArity
entries.summary: Merges curried layers until the type takes `arity` arguments: `FilePath -> Read -> Mode -> R` with arity 3 becomes `(FilePath, Read, Mode) -> R`. A type that runs out of layers, or whose next layer would overshoot, is left as it is.

entries.name: clauseParams
entries.summary: Returns a clause's parameters, leaving out a receiver pattern: in `let factor(@Nanosecond) = ...` the pattern picks the clause and is not something a caller passes.

entries.name: qualify
entries.summary: Prefixes `name` with its parent module's name. A module may be written fully qualified (`module FS.File do` inside `module FS do`), so a name that already starts with the prefix is left alone.

entries.name: submodulesHtml
entries.summary:
Lists the pages nested under this one, each with its module's summary.

A module family spread over several files (net.kex, net/dns.kex, net/http.kex, ...) gets one page per file, and without this list the "Net" page would not show that Net.DNS or Net.Socket exist.

entries.summary:
Links a `using X` line of prelude.kex to the page of the file it names.

It matches the file, not the link index or the page title: in the index, `Map`, `Set` and `Range` are each claimed by a module and a type, so they would not link, and `using Test` is test.kex, whose page is titled "Assert".

entries.name: versionIndexHtml
entries.summary: Renders <pkg>/<version>/index.html, with a card for every module. When the package has a prelude, the cards are split into the modules it makes visible and those that need a `using`.

entries.name: cardModules
entries.summary: Returns the modules that get a card. Modules holding only constants are left out (`Int8`, `Float32` and the like, which are on number.kex's page), as are modules declared in more than one place.

entries.name: preludePaths
entries.summary:
Returns the pages of the files the prelude imports.

The prelude imports files, and everything in a file comes with it: `using Time` is what brings `Date`, `Duration` and `Time.Period` into scope, though prelude.kex names none of them. So the split is by page, not by module name.

entries.name: latestVersion
entries.summary:
Returns the version a reader gets by default: the highest release by semantic version, and a `-dev` build only when there is no release.

versions.json is in build order, newest first, and tools/build-docs.sh builds the working tree last, so its first entry is usually the `-dev` build.

entries.name: versionsNewestFirst
entries.summary: Returns one package's versions, highest semantic version first.

entries.name: packageRedirectHtml
entries.summary: Renders <pkg>/index.html, which redirects to the latest version, or lists the versions when there is no release to pick. The other versions are listed at versions.html.

entries.name: packageVersionsHtml
entries.summary: Renders <pkg>/versions.html, listing one package's versions, newest first. A version id is whatever the package uses: a library's own releases, or the Kex release for the stdlib.

entries.name: searchPageHtml
entries.summary: Renders <pkg>/<version>/search.html, the full-page search. The search box on every page links here with `?q=<term>`, so a page of results has a URL that can be shared.

entries.name: rootIndexHtml
entries.summary: Renders the site's root index.html, with one card per package for its newest build. It is built from every entry in versions.json, so it lists packages from earlier builds too.

entries.name: packageNames
entries.summary: Returns the package names in the order they first appear. Versions come newest first from `accumulateVersions`, so that is the order of each package's newest build.

entries.name: chrome
signatures: chrome(title: String, root: String, script: Bool, nav: String, content: String) -> String
entries.summary: Wraps `content` in what every full page shares: the `<head>` and the top bar, with the brand on the left and `nav` on the right. `root` is the relative path to the site root, and `script` says whether the page loads assets/site.js.

A page whose title extends another page's title nests under it ("Net.DNS" under "Net", "Net.HTTP.WebSocket" under "Net.HTTP"), so a module spread over several files reads as one branch. The current page expands to its top-level declarations. The heading is the package name and links to the version index.

Returns the names documented by other units, read from the comma-separated model.json files in `paths`, so this unit's signatures and prose can link to them.

The Tey reference uses this to link `String` and `FS.Path` to the standard library. Each model.json names its package and version, and its pages are linked at ../../<package>/<version>/ from this unit's version directory. A file that cannot be read or is not JSON is reported as a warning and skipped.

entries.summary:

The page shows the signature's type either way; the note says which comment has fallen behind its code.

entries.name: preludeInfo
entries.summary:
Returns the prelude of the source tree at `source`: the file name, the modules it makes visible, and its opening comment.

A `prelude.kex` is an opening comment followed by one bare `using <Module>` per line, so reading the lines is enough. Without one the result is `("", [], "")` and the output never mentions a prelude.

entries.name: leadingComment
entries.summary: Returns the comment lines at the top of `lines` with their `#` markers removed, ready for the same parse as any other doc comment.

entries.name: fileHeader
entries.summary:
Returns the file's opening comment when a blank line follows it, and `""` otherwise.

A comment that runs straight into a declaration is that declaration's doc, and the page gets no introduction. A `#!` line does not count as a comment.

entries.name: usingName
entries.summary: Returns the module a `using` line names (`"using List"` gives `"List"`), or `""` for any other line.

entries.name: defaultSource
entries.summary: Returns `given` when it is not empty, else `"src"` when the current directory has one, else `""`, which the scan reports as having no .kex files.

entries.name: defaultPackage
entries.summary:
Returns `given` when it is not empty, else the name in the current directory's package.kex, else `""`.

With `""`, `buildCommand` stops with an error and asks for `--package`; it does not invent a name (kexhq/kex#287).

entries.name: defaultVersion
entries.summary:
Returns `given` when it is not empty, else the version in the current directory's package.kex, else `""`.

Outside a package the caller must pass `--release`: what a version means differs between units, such as a library's releases and the standard library's Kex releases.

entries.name: manifestVersion
entries.summary: Returns the name and version from the current directory's package.kex, or `None` when there is none or it does not parse.

entries.name: Frontmatter
entries.summary: The frontmatter keys this reader uses. Other keys are ignored, so a page may carry metadata for something else.

entries.name: ListItem
entries.summary: One item of a list: its own inline text, plus any blocks nested under it.

entries.name: MdBlock
entries.summary: A block of a Markdown document.

entries.name: Document
entries.summary: A parsed document: its frontmatter and its blocks.

entries.name: parseDocument
entries.summary: Parses a Markdown document. Windows line endings are accepted.

entries.name: toHtml
entries.summary: Returns the HTML for a document's body, ignoring its frontmatter.

entries.name: splitFrontmatter
entries.summary:
--- frontmatter -------------------------------------------------------

A leading `---` fence delimits frontmatter. Without one the document is all body, and every field takes its default.

entries.name: assign
signatures: assign(front: Frontmatter, key: String, value: String) -> Frontmatter

entries.name: trimEnds
entries.summary: Drops the first and last character, the quotes `quoted?` matched.

entries.name: blockLoop
entries.summary: One pass over the lines, each branch consuming the whole construct it recognises and returning the lines it did not take.

entries.name: rule?
entries.summary: Returns `true` for a horizontal rule: three or more of `-`, `*` or `_` and nothing else on the line. Frontmatter is removed before this runs.

entries.name: headingLevel
entries.summary: Returns a heading's level, so `##` gives 2, or 0 when the line is not a heading. `#hashtag` is not one.

entries.name: takeCode
entries.summary:
--- fenced code -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a fenced code block. The word after the fence is the language. A fence that is never closed runs to the end of the document.

entries.name: takeQuote
entries.summary:
--- blockquotes -------------------------------------------------------

Takes a blockquote. The `>` is stripped from each line and the rest is parsed as blocks, so a quote can hold anything a document can.

entries.name: takeList
entries.summary:
--- lists -------------------------------------------------------------

Takes a list. A line indented past the first item's marker belongs to the item above it and is parsed as blocks, so an item can hold paragraphs, code and nested lists.

entries.name: listLine?
entries.summary: Returns `true` for a line that can continue a list: an item, an indented line or a blank line. The first other line ends the list.

entries.name: flushItem
entries.summary: Adds the collected item to `accum`. The first line is the item's text; the lines below it are dedented and parsed as nested blocks.

entries.name: dedent
entries.summary: Removes the common indent, so nested content is parsed at column zero.

entries.name: numberMarker
entries.summary: Returns a numbered-list marker, so `"12. "` gives `"12."`, or `""` when the line has none.

entries.name: tableStart?
entries.summary:
--- tables ------------------------------------------------------------

Returns `true` when the lines start a GFM table: a header row followed by a row of dashes. Without that row the lines are a paragraph.

entries.name: cellsOf
entries.summary: Returns the cells of a table row. Leading and trailing pipes are optional.

entries.name: takeParagraph
entries.summary:
--- paragraphs --------------------------------------------------------

Takes a paragraph, which ends at a blank line or where another block starts, so a list or code fence right under prose is not swallowed.

entries.name: renderCode
entries.summary: Renders a code block. Kex code goes through the reference pages' highlighter; other languages are escaped and left plain.

entries.name: anchor
entries.summary: Returns a heading's id: lower case, with each run of characters other than letters and digits turned into one dash.

entries.name: trimDashes
entries.summary: Removes dashes from both ends, which `anchor` can leave: `(try)` becomes `-try-` before this.

entries.name: stripInline
entries.summary: Returns the text with the inline markers (backticks, `*` and `_`) removed.

entries.name: inline
entries.summary:
--- inline ------------------------------------------------------------

Renders inline Markdown. Code spans are handled first: their content is escaped but not scanned for emphasis, so `a*b*c` in backticks stays as written.

entries.name: emphasis
entries.summary: Renders links, then bold and italics, so a `*` inside a URL is not read as a marker.

entries.name: linkParts
entries.summary: Splits `label](href)` and what follows it into `(label, href, rest)`, or returns `None` when it is not a link, and the `[` is plain text.

entries.name: marks
entries.summary: Renders bold before italics, or the opening `**` would be read as empty italics. The remaining text is escaped here.

entries.name: wrap

entries.name: pairs
signatures: pairs(text: String, mark: String, tag: String, accum: String) -> String
entries.summary: Replaces each pair of markers with a tag. A marker without a partner is left as written.

entries.name: indexOfText
signatures: indexOfText(haystack: String, needle: String, at: Integer) -> Integer?
entries.summary: Returns where `needle` first occurs in `haystack` from `at` on, or `None`. `String.indexOf` only finds a `Char`, and `**` is two characters.

entries.name: Extension
entries.summary:
One `make` block as seen from the type it extends: where it is, the names it adds and the traits it declares.

A type's functions can be spread over many files (there is a `make Integer` in number.kex, period.kex, units.kex and others), and these rows gather them on the type's page.

entries.name: TypeFacts
entries.summary:
Everything the package says about one type, across files.

`homePath` is the type's main page: the one declaring it, or for a builtin such as Integer or String the one named after it.

entries.name: TraitFacts
entries.summary: A trait seen from the outside: where it is documented and which make blocks implement it.

entries.name: ModuleIndexEntry
entries.summary:
One module of the package and the page its entities are on.

The sidebar and the module index of model.json are built from these. Readers navigate by module, and a module need not match a file.

entries.name: MemberEntry
entries.summary: One documented member of a module and the anchor of its section, for the sidebar and the JSON index.

entries.name: LinkEntry
entries.summary: One row of the cross-link index: a name that a type reference may mention, such as "String" or "FS.Path", and where it links to. Every renderer resolves names against this one list.

entries.name: PackageModel
entries.summary: Everything extracted from one package: its pages, modules, links and cross-file relations.

entries.name: SearchEntry
entries.summary:
One row of the search index, for an entity or for a function inside a trait, make or module.

`types` are the type names its signature mentions, so a search can match by type as well as by name. `anchor` is the section a result links to.

entries.name: VersionEntry
entries.summary: One row of versions.json. Each build adds or replaces its own `(package, id)` row in the file already in the output directory, so the file lists every version built there.

entries.name: kindOf
entries.summary: Returns the kind label an entity has in indexes and JSON, such as `"record"` or `"make"`.

entries.name: nameOf
entries.summary: Returns an entity's display name; a make's is its target type.

entries.name: anchorOf
entries.summary:
Returns the id of an entity's HTML section.

It is here, not in the HTML renderer, because the cross-link index and the sidebar need the same ids.

entries.name: anchorNameOf
entries.summary: Returns the text an entity's anchor is made from: a make's full target, type parameters included, or otherwise the qualified name.

entries.name: memberAnchorOf
entries.summary: Returns the anchor of a function documented inside a trait or make section. It includes the owner, because one page can hold several owners with a `count`, such as `[X]` and `String`.

entries.name: ownerSlugOf
entries.summary: Returns the slug of an owner type: `[X]` gives "list", `[Number]` gives "list-number" and `FileHandle<CanRead, W>` gives "filehandle-canread". Type variables (a capital letter, optionally followed by a digit) are dropped.

entries.name: wordsOf
entries.summary: Returns the runs of letters, digits, `_`, `?` and `!` in a type's text.

entries.name: slugOf
entries.summary: Returns a name spelled for an HTML id: lower case, with each run of punctuation turned into one dash. `?` and `!` are kept, as in `empty?`.

entries.name: operatorSlug
entries.summary: Returns the slug of an operator, which has no letters of its own: `<=>` gives "op-lt-eq-gt" and a plus sign "op-plus".

entries.name: baseTypeOf
entries.summary: Returns the type a make block extends, without its type arguments: "[X]" gives "List", "{K: V}" and "Map<K, V>" give "Map", and "FileHandle<R, W>" gives "FileHandle".
